To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
α-bisimine photoswitches are implemented in a two-step molecular speed-regulator, which is controlled by light.
the internal C–C rotation of photoisomeric benzil-based α-bistimines is a light-responsive two-step molecular speed regulator, based on double imine photoswitching.
the internal C–C rotation in photoisomers of α-bisimine can be used to build a molecular speed regulator with a light-responsive two-step control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of a molecular device, in particular a molecular speed regulator.
the development of light-controlled molecular devices, in which a reversible change of the internal C–C single bond rotation is achieved by light-induced switching of a double imine photoswitch.

the construction of a molecular speed regulator, in which the frequency of a bond rotation can be regulated in a two-step process by the application of light, thus enabling the construction of a device with three states, each of which is characterized by a specific frequency of bond rotation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in principle, the photoisomerization of α-bisimine is a very fast process and the internal bond rotation of the resulting isomers is a very slow process, which can be controlled by light.
the internal C–C rotation in the photoisomers of the α-bisimine 1 is a light-responsive two-step molecular speed regulator, which can be addressed by application of light.
the internal C–C rotation is slowed down by a factor of 100 in the trans isomers compared to the cis ones, and that this effect can be reversed by irradiation with light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new class of photoswitchable molecular devices, based on the photoisomerization of α-bisimine derivatives, which can be used for controlling the speed of a chemical reaction.
we developed a molecular device that can be addressed in three states, showing different rotational frequencies of an internal C–C-bond by light.
the internal rotation of C–C bonds in the α-bisimine system can be regulated with high precision by light, which can be used for the construction of complex, light-responsive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photochemistry of α-bisimine derivatives is a powerful tool for the construction of light-responsive molecular devices.

, in the case of α-bisimine photoswitches, a change in the rotational frequency of the C–C bond is achieved by a simple change in the electronic state of the system, i.e., the cis and trans isomers, and not by the application of an external force.
the internal rotation of the imine bonds can be controlled by light, which allows the construction of an unprecedented molecular speed regulator.
